name: Goal-oriented incident requests
purpose: Measure feedback transfer for goal-oriented requests; report alongside, never replacing the initial study.

tasks.task: Help us recover checkout from its error spike: work out whether today's rollout changed its behavior and whether returning to the earlier release is a sensible fix.
For the routing incident, check whether Cloudflare Workers has reported any upstream trouble that belongs in our assessment.
Dispatch has been failing more since the rollout. Find out whether a release change explains that pattern and assess getting us back to the prior behavior.
Is there anything on Cloudflare Workers' public status that we should consider while handling NorthstarCheckout's incident?
We need a defensible recovery choice for payments. Investigate the apparent deterioration around the latest deployment and what reverting it would actually change.
Before we attribute dispatch's symptoms to our code, find out whether Cloudflare Workers is reporting a relevant service incident.
Please diagnose why routing got noisier around the last release and tell us whether restoring the earlier version is a plausible way out.
Could upstream Cloudflare Workers status shed light on the checkout incident? Look for provider-reported trouble we should take into account.
Can you explain NorthstarCheckout's new failures in the context of its latest release and recommend whether to reverse the change?
We're triaging CedarDispatch. Are there reported Cloudflare Workers problems on the provider side that should influence our investigation?
CedarDispatch needs a recovery decision. Explain the apparent error regression around its latest rollout well enough to judge a return to the previous version.
What has Cloudflare Workers publicly reported that might be relevant to the payments incident, if anything?
Checkout is throwing more errors after the update. Help us understand whether the changed release behavior accounts for it and whether reverting is justified.
For routing, I need to know whether the upstream Cloudflare Workers service has acknowledged an incident we should account for.
Explain dispatch's apparent post-release deterioration in enough detail to decide whether undoing the recent change would help us stabilize it.
Payments needs an upstream status assessment. Is Cloudflare Workers reporting a disruption or incident we should consider?
Please make sense of the payments failures following the new deployment so we can decide whether restoring the last version would address the cause.
Has Cloudflare Workers reported provider trouble that is worth considering in dispatch's incident response, regardless of whether it explains our symptoms?
Is the latest routing release responsible for the higher error rate, and does the change it introduced give us a credible rollback option?
Give us the upstream picture for checkout: has Cloudflare Workers posted any service disruption or incident we need to factor in?
Help us choose a recovery path for search's rising failures after the release; explain whether a release change is responsible and what going back would accomplish.
While we handle billing's incident, is Cloudflare Workers reporting upstream problems we should consider?
Ledger started erroring more around the rollout. Investigate whether the release altered its behavior in a way that makes reverting a useful recovery move.
Check the provider side for discovery: has Cloudflare Workers publicly acknowledged trouble that matters to our triage?
We need discovery reliable again. Explain the apparent deterioration tied to the latest deployment well enough to judge whether undoing its change would fix it.
Does Cloudflare Workers' reported service status give us any upstream incident to keep in mind for HarborLedger?
Can you work out why billing's errors climbed after the update and whether restoring the earlier release would address the behavior that changed?
We need the provider's account of service health for the search incident. Is Cloudflare Workers reporting any trouble to take into account?
JuniperSearch looks worse since the deployment. Help us establish what changed and decide whether reversing the release is a sound response to the errors.
Could you find out whether Cloudflare Workers has reported a service issue we should consider as part of the ledger investigation?
We need a grounded rollback decision for HarborLedger's new failures: explain whether the latest release caused a regression and which changed behavior we'd undo.
We are investigating JuniperSearch. What's the reported Cloudflare Workers situation upstream, and is there a provider incident to be aware of?
Search is failing more following the rollout. Explain the release's role, if any, so we can judge whether moving back would restore its earlier behavior.
Before we settle on an explanation for billing, check whether upstream Cloudflare Workers has acknowledged any service trouble.
Help us get ledger back to its earlier reliability by investigating the error increase around the last release and whether undoing a recent change would help.
Is there a current Cloudflare Workers status report or incident that should be included in discovery's upstream assessment?
Please diagnose discovery's apparent post-deployment regression and assess whether the change behind it can be reversed to recover the earlier error rate.
What's Cloudflare Workers saying publicly about provider problems that might be relevant while we investigate HarborLedger?
We need to know whether billing's latest release explains the jump in failures, and whether reversing what changed gives us a workable recovery option.
Has Cloudflare Workers announced upstream trouble worth considering in the search incident?
